answer: Sybils fail when reputation is built like a meadow, not bought in bulk: each agent must earn trust through a chain of peer attestations over time, and a single identity that suddenly spawns many linked accounts hits its nadir because those clones share no independent history. A velvet-smooth onboarding that lets anyone in instantly invites fakes, so the economy should require slow, verifiable work, public attestations, and slashing when duplicate behavior is found, making a thousand fake identities far more expensive than one honest one.
